mainTopic: How the sex of a טומטום is determined (in a בכור animal and in a person), the principle הואיל ואישתני אישתני, and the ברייתות about a טומטום's widow and יבום.
overview: The גמרא first rejects the idea that רבי שמעון בן יהודה sees a טומטום as a separate creature. Everyone agrees it is only a doubt between male and female. The real dispute is about a טומטום animal that urinates from the female place. רבי אלעזר ruled that such an animal is חולין. רבי יוחנן objected that this follows one opinion against two. רבי אלעזר's reasoning comes from ריש לקיש: in an animal, the place of urination shows its sex. רב אושעיא worries that the organ may be reversed, which leads to the principle הואיל ואישתני אישתני. The גמרא tries to find that principle in two ברייתות about the widow of a טומטום and יבום. It concludes that the ברייתות really follow רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה as the author who treats a טומטום as only possibly a סריס חמה. The amud ends as רבא begins to explain how רבי יהודה and his son differ.

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון בן יהודה say a טומטום is a separate creature?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון בן יהודה means a טומטום is its own kind of creature and is therefore not holy as a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does [רבי שמעון] בן יהודה come to say that a טומטום is a separate creature, and so it is not holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out one possible reading of רבי שמעון בן יהודה's view that a טומטום בכור is not holy. It asks whether his reason is that a טומטום is a totally separate kind of creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is only holy if it is a definite male. If a טומטום were a third category, neither male nor female, it could never become holy. The גמרא raises this reading so it can test it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A person or animal whose genitals are covered, so we cannot tell if it is male or female
A creature; here, a separate category of its own
Holy (here, having the holiness of a בכור)
To say; 'does he come to say'

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of the name רבי שמעון בן יהודה. The words בן יהודה finish a sentence that started at the end of the previous amud.

phrases.english: [Does Rabbi Shimon] ben Yehuda come to say:
phrases.notes: Continues the name from the end of the previous amud

phrases.english: A tumtum is a separate creature, and it is not holy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of רבי שמעון בן יהודה's view, which was quoted on the previous amud
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the reason a טומטום is not holy that it is a separate creature, neither male nor female?

steps.title: No: everyone agrees a טומטום is only a male-or-female doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Nobody holds that a טומטום is a separate creature. The only question is whether it is male or female.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that a טומטום is not in doubt about being a separate creature. The only doubt is whether it is male or female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers 'no' to the suggestion in step 1. All opinions agree a טומטום is not a third kind of creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the argument. A טומטום really is either male or female; we just cannot see which. So רבי שמעון בן יהודה's reason must be something else, which the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone; all opinions agree
It is in doubt
Male and female

phrases.english: No, for according to everyone,
about a tumtum being a separate creature, there is no doubt [that it is not];
whether it is male or female, that is what is in doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading proposed in step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No one holds a טומטום is a separate creature; the only doubt is male versus female.

steps.title: The real argument: a טומטום that urinates from the female place
steps.stepSummary: If the טומטום urinates from the male place, everyone agrees it is male. The argument is about one that urinates from the female place. One side worries that the male organ is turned inward; the other side does not worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it urinates from the male place, everyone agrees it is a male. They argue about one that urinates from the female place. One master holds that we worry the male organ may have turned toward the female place. The other master holds that we do not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explains what רבי שמעון בן יהודה and the רבנן really argue about. It is a case where the signs point toward female.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say that even urinating from the female place does not prove female status, since a hidden male organ might be turned that way. So for them the animal stays a doubt. רבי שמעון בן יהודה relies on the sign and treats it as female, so the בכור is not holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Urinates
The male organ
The female organ
We are concerned; we take the possibility into account
Was turned over or inverted

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the argument from a question about categories into a question of how much we trust a physical sign. That is a much smaller and more practical dispute.

phrases.english: If it urinates from the place of the male organ,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּזָכָר הוּא,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that it is a male.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּמֵטִיל מַיִם בְּמָקוֹם נַקְבוּת:
phrases.english: Where they argue is when it urinates from the place of the female organ:
One master holds that we are concerned
that perhaps its male organ was turned toward its female place;
phrases.notes: This is the view of the רבנן, so the animal remains a doubt

phrases.english: and the other master holds that we are not concerned.
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון בן יהודה, so the animal is a definite female

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the real dispute after step 2 rejected the 'separate creature' reading
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urinating from the male place means definitely male. From the female place, the רבנן worry the organ is inverted, so it is a doubt; רבי שמעון בן יהודה does not worry, so it is female.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ruled like רבי שמעון בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ruled that an animal that urinates from the female place is חולין, not holy. This matches the view that we do not worry about an inverted organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רבי אלעזר ruled: an animal that urinates from the female place is חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real ruling of רבי אלעזר that follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה's approach. This ruling also sets up רבי יוחנן's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר trusts the sign of urinating from the female place, so he treats the animal as female. A female cannot be a בכור, so it is חולין. This shows the view of רבי שמעון בן יהודה was actually applied in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Ruled; gave a practical ruling
Animal
Not holy; ordinary

phrases.english: Like that which Rabbi Elazar ruled:

phrases.aramaic: בִּבְהֵמָה מֵטִיל מַיִם בְּמָקוֹם נַקְבוּת — חוּלִּין.
phrases.english: For an animal that urinates from the place of the female organ, it is non-holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling that follows the 'not concerned' view from step 3
steps.raayaObject: The view that we are not concerned about an inverted organ
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's practical ruling about an animal

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is surprised at רבי אלעזר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן wonders how רבי אלעזר could ignore the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל, who both treat a טומטום as a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן wondered about it: who is it that does not care about the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling. Two opinions in the משנה treat a טומטום as a doubt, so how could רבי אלעזר rule against them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל both hold that a טומטום is a doubt and might be male. Ruling that it is plain חולין goes against both of them. רבי יוחנן finds it strange to ignore them.

keyTerms.meaning: Wondered about it; was surprised by it
Cared about; took into account
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan wondered about it:
Who is it that is not concerned about the first tanna
and about Rabbi Yishmael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רבי אלעזר from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that the animal is חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It goes against two תנאים who treat a טומטום as a doubt.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי יוחנן also mention the רבנן בתראי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not also list the later רבנן. According to רב חסדא, they too hold that a טומטום is a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי יוחנן also say: who is it that does not care about the later רבנן? For רב חסדא said: the argument is about an אנדרוגינוס, but about a טומטום everyone agrees it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions רבי יוחנן's own words. If רב חסדא is right, there was a third opinion against רבי אלעזר, so why name only two?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא limits the later רבנן's ruling to an אנדרוגינוס. That means for a טומטום, they also hold it is a doubt. So רבי יוחנן's list seems to be missing one.

keyTerms.meaning: The later רבנן, the Sages who speak at the end of the משנה
One with both male and female organs
Everyone agrees
A doubtful case

phrases.english: But let Rabbi Yochanan also say:
Who is it that is not concerned about the later Rabbis?
For Rav Chisda said:
The dispute is about a hermaphrodite;
but about a tumtum, everyone agrees it is a doubt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי יוחנן's surprise in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן listing only two opinions
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב חסדא, the רבנן בתראי also hold that a טומטום is a doubt, so they should have been listed too.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן does not accept רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב חסדא. In his view, the רבנן בתראי do not treat a טומטום as a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן does not hold like רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 6. רבי יוחנן did not list the רבנן בתראי because he does not read them the way רב חסדא does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the later רבנן's ruling also covers a טומטום, so they agree with רבי אלעזר. That is why רבי יוחנן left them out of the list of opponents.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold like that

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan does not hold like Rav Chisda.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise that רב חסדא's reading applies to רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן בתראי also hold that a טומטום is a doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוחנן, the רבנן בתראי agree with רבי אלעזר's approach.

steps.title: Then why was רבי יוחנן surprised at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן בתראי agree with רבי אלעזר, רבי יוחנן should simply say that רבי אלעזר follows them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he does not hold like רב חסדא, let him say that רבי אלעזר ruled like the later רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer in step 7. If רבי אלעזר has a משנה opinion behind him, there seems to be nothing to wonder about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבי יוחנן admits that the רבנן בתראי support רבי אלעזר, רבי אלעזר is just following a valid opinion. So why call his ruling strange?

keyTerms.meaning: If
Let him say

phrases.english: If he does not hold like him,
let him say that he [Rabbi Elazar] spoke in accordance with the later Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's surprise at רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an opinion in the משנה supports רבי אלעזר, his ruling is not surprising.

steps.title: That is the point: why follow one opinion against two?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's surprise was exactly this: רבי אלעזר left the two opinions of the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל and followed only the one opinion of the רבנן בתראי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is indeed what he is saying: who leaves two and acts like one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 8 and closes this discussion. רבי יוחנן knew רבי אלעזר had support, but he was surprised that רבי אלעזר chose the minority side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we follow the majority. Two opinions, the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל, say a טומטום is a doubt, and only one says otherwise. רבי יוחנן's question was why רבי אלעזר left the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: That is indeed what he is saying
Leaves aside
Two
Like one

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees a טומטום is a doubt between male and female, not a separate creature. רבי שמעון בן יהודה and רבי אלעזר trust urinating from the female place as a sign of female. רבי יוחנן objected that this follows one opinion (the רבנן בתראי) against two (the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן never said that רבי אלעזר had no source. His complaint is only that רבי אלעזר followed a minority of one against two.

phrases.english: That is indeed what he is saying:
Who leaves aside two and acts in accordance with one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by reinterpreting רבי יוחנן's surprise in step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's surprise was about following a minority of one against a majority of two, not about רבי אלעזר having no source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets רבי יוחנן's surprise: it was about following one opinion against two, not about רבי אלעזר lacking a source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the רבנן בתראי support רבי אלעזר, רבי יוחנן had nothing to wonder about.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's wonder was precisely that רבי אלעזר left the majority of two (תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל) to follow one (the רבנן בתראי).

steps.title: What is the reasoning behind רבי אלעזר's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which reasoning or source רבי אלעזר relies on when he says a טומטום animal is not treated as a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר, whose view does he follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי אלעזר's position. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that רבי אלעזר sides with the רבנן בתראי. Now the גמרא wants the logic: why should a טומטום animal not be a ספק when a human טומטום is one? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does he hold? (asking for someone's reasoning or source)
A creature whose sex organs are covered, so its sex is unknown
A doubt; a case whose status is uncertain

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar, in accordance with whom does he hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that רבי אלעזר follows the רבנן בתראי, and now asks for the underlying logic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind treating a טומטום animal as not being a doubt.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: an animal's sex can be told by where it urinates
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that a טומטום is a doubt only for humans, because human male and female organs are in the same area. An animal's sex can be determined by the place it urinates from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like what ריש לקיש said: they only called a טומטום a doubt for a person, because a person's male and female organs are in one place. But an animal that urinates from the male area is male, and one that urinates from the female area is female.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר follows ריש לקיש's rule. A human טומטום is a doubt, but an animal טומטום is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a human, both organs are in the same area, so if that area is covered we cannot tell the sex. In an animal, the male and female openings are in different places on the body. So where the animal urinates from tells us its sex, even if the organ itself is covered.

keyTerms.meaning: Its male organ and its female organ
In one place (the same area of the body)
Urinates
Since; because

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for the next part of the סוגיא. רב אושעיא's challenge, and the debate over הואיל ואישתני אישתני that follows, are aimed at it.

phrases.english: Like that which Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמְרוּ טוּמְטוּם סָפֵק אֶלָּא בְּאָדָם,
phrases.english: They said a tumtum is a doubt only regarding a person,
since its male and female organs are in one place,
but an animal —
if it urinates from the male place, it is male;
if it urinates from the female place, it is female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר follows ריש לקיש: the doubt applies only to humans, while an animal's sex is known from where it urinates.

steps.title: רב אושעיא: maybe the animal's organ is reversed
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא challenges ריש לקיש. Perhaps this animal's male organ was turned around toward the female area, so urination would mislead us.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא objected: let us worry that perhaps its male organ was reversed to its female place!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא attacks ריש לקיש's test. He argues that the place of urination might not be reliable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's whole rule depends on the organs being in their normal places. רב אושעיא suggests that in this animal they could be reversed. If so, urinating from the female area would not prove it is female.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it (a strong challenge)
And let us be concerned
Was turned around / reversed

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya objected to it:
Let us be concerned that perhaps its male organ was reversed toward its female place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the urination test from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that an animal's sex is decided by the place of urination.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The test only works if the organs are in their usual position, and they might be reversed.

steps.title: Worrying about rare cases follows only רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The reply to רב אושעיא: your worry follows רבי מאיר, who is concerned about a minority. We do not rule like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: according to whom are you asking? According to רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority?!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone (according to the Sefaria translation, אביי) defends ריש לקיש. He says רב אושעיא's worry about a reversed organ is too rare to matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals with reversed organs are very rare, a מיעוטא. Only רבי מאיר takes such a minority into account. The הלכה follows the רבנן, who go by the majority, so the urination test stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He is concerned about the minority (rare cases)
The תנא known for worrying about minority cases

steps.confusionAlert: This does not deny that a reversed organ can ever happen. It only says that the הלכה does not worry about such a rare case.

phrases.english: He said to him: In accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Meir, who is concerned about the minority?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּחָיֵישׁ לְמִיעוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by tying it to a minority opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the challenge to a view (רבי מאיר) that the הלכה does not follow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A reversed organ is a real concern that undermines the urination test.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a rare minority case, and only רבי מאיר worries about such cases.

steps.title: Even the רבנן might worry: once unusual, maybe unusual again
steps.stepSummary: אביי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין defend רב אושעיא even according to the רבנן. Since this animal is already abnormal (a טומטום), it may be abnormal in other ways too. They add that this principle is itself disputed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי בר אבין and רב חנניא בר אבין both said: you can even say this follows the רבנן, since it has changed, it has changed. Some say we assume it changed, and some say we do not assume it changed.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים rescue רב אושעיא's worry. They show it does not have to depend on רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the רבנן follow the majority. But this animal has already left the majority by being a טומטום, so we cannot assume it is normal in other ways. Then they note that the principle הואיל ואישתני אישתני is debated: some accept it and some do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
You can even say it follows the רבנן
Since it changed (in one way), it may have changed (in another way)
There are those who say

steps.whatToRemember: The key new idea is הואיל ואישתני אישתני. A creature that is already abnormal loses the assumption that it matches the majority, and this idea is debated.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַב חֲנַנְיָא בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: Abaye bar Avin and Rav Ḥananya bar Avin
both of them say:
You may even say it follows the Rabbis,
since it has changed, it has changed.
There are those who say it has changed,
and there are those who say it has not changed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, הוֹאִיל וְאִישְׁתַּנִּי אִישְׁתַּנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 13's claim that רב אושעיא must follow רבי מאיר, and restores his challenge on new grounds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Provides a new principle, so the challenge works even according to the רבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Worrying about a reversed organ requires רבי מאיר's concern for the minority.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the רבנן may worry, because an already abnormal animal is not presumed to follow the majority, though this point is disputed.

steps.title: Is this principle a dispute between תנאים? A ברייתא on a טומטום's betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the dispute over הואיל ואישתני אישתני may be a disagreement between תנאים. It starts quoting a ברייתא: a טומטום who betroths a woman, or who is betrothed by a man, has a valid קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that 'it changed' and 'it did not change' is a dispute between תנאים? As it was taught: a טומטום who betrothed a woman, the betrothal is valid; if the טומטום was betrothed, the betrothal is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes finding the dispute about הואיל ואישתני אישתני in an earlier source. It starts quoting a ברייתא, setting up the analysis that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats a human טומטום as a doubt in both directions. Its קידושין counts whether it gives or receives, since it might be male or female. The גמרא will look for a later part of the ברייתא or a contrasting opinion that relates to the idea of 'once changed, changed'.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggested proposal)
A dispute between תנאים
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Betrothal
Was betrothed (received betrothal)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. Step 16 completes it, and step 18 shows its connection to the 'changed' dispute.

phrases.english: Shall we say that 'it changed' and 'it did not change' is a dispute of tanna'im?
As it is taught in a baraita:
A tumtum who betrothed — his betrothal is a betrothal;
was betrothed — the betrothal is a betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the dispute named in step 14 and searches for it in a ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute over הואיל ואישתני אישתני already appears as a disagreement among תנאים.

steps.title: Two ברייתות on a טומטום and יבום
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא continues: a טומטום does חליצה, and his brothers may do either חליצה or יבום with his widow. A second ברייתא says the widow of a טומטום does חליצה but not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first ברייתא continues: a טומטום performs חליצה. If he dies, his brothers may do חליצה with his wife or marry her through יבום. Another ברייתא teaches: the wife of a טומטום does חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the first ברייתא and then places a second ברייתא beside it that seems to disagree. It is setting up two sources so it can compare them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that a טומטום might be a male, so his widow needs some release from the brothers. The difference is about יבום. The first ברייתא allows it. The second allows only חליצה, which means it has some extra worry about this טומטום.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a childless widow from her husband's brother without marriage
The brother of a man who died childless marries the widow
"Another ברייתא teaches." It introduces a second, contrasting source.
The wife of a person whose sex is hidden and unknown

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the first line is a new source. It is the end of the same ברייתא that began in step 15 (a טומטום who betroths a woman).

phrases.english: And he performs ḥalitza, and they perform ḥalitza with his wife,
phrases.notes: Continuation of the first ברייתא

phrases.english: and they may perform levirate marriage with his wife.
And another baraita teaches:
The wife of a tumtum performs ḥalitza
and does not enter levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 15 and adds a contrasting ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The proposal that הואיל ואישתני אישתני is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות that disagree about whether the widow of a טומטום may do יבום

steps.title: Assumption That Both Follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes both ברייתות follow רבי עקיבא, who says a סריס חמה neither does חליצה nor יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that everyone holds like רבי עקיבא, who says: a סריס חמה (someone infertile from birth) does not do חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a working assumption that both ברייתות agree with רבי עקיבא. This is a setup line that prepares the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, a סריס חמה is completely outside the מצוה of יבום. His widow is simply forbidden to his brothers as a brother's wife. So if there is any doubt that a man is a סריס חמה, יבום becomes risky.

keyTerms.meaning: "They assumed." A working assumption that may later be questioned.
Everyone; all opinions involved
A person infertile from birth (natural eunuch)
The תנא whose view on סריס חמה is used here

steps.confusionAlert: The word סברוה signals an assumption, not a final conclusion. The גמרא often uses it right before it later rejects the assumption.

phrases.english: They assumed that everyone holds like Rabbi Akiva,
who says: a eunuch from birth
does not perform ḥalitza and does not perform levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the shared background assumption needed to read the two ברייתות as a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both ברייתות are assumed to follow רבי עקיבא: a סריס חמה is excluded from חליצה and יבום.

steps.title: Do the ברייתות argue about הואיל ואישתני אישתני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתות disagree about הואיל ואישתני אישתני. One does not worry that the טומטום may also be a סריס חמה, so it allows יבום. The other does worry, so it allows only חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this? The one who says he does חליצה, and the brothers may do חליצה or יבום with his wife, holds that we do not say "since he changed, he changed." The one who says the wife does חליצה but not יבום holds that we do say "since he changed, he changed."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the two ברייתות are really arguing about the principle הואיל ואישתני אישתני. That would make it a dispute between תנאים, which answers the suggestion raised in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא assumes that if the טומטום is male, he is a normal, fertile male, so יבום is allowed. The second ברייתא worries that since he is already unusual, he might also be a סריס חמה. Under רבי עקיבא, his widow would then be forbidden to the brothers, so יבום is blocked. Only חליצה remains, in case he was a normal male.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is it not that...?" It introduces a proposed explanation.
They disagree
"Since it changed, it changed." Something abnormal in one way may be abnormal in other ways.
We say; we apply the principle

steps.whatToRemember: The proposal is this: the ברייתא that allows יבום does not apply הואיל ואישתני אישתני. The ברייתא that forbids יבום does apply it. This would make רב אושעיא's principle a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this is a dispute between תנאים, then the defense of רב אושעיא in step 14 rests on one side of an argument between תנאים.

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:
that the one who says he performs ḥalitza,
and they perform ḥalitza with his wife and may perform levirate marriage with his wife,
holds that we do not say
"since it changed, it changed";
and the one who says she performs ḥalitza and does not enter levirate marriage
holds that we say "since it changed, it changed"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the רבי עקיבא assumption from step 17 to explain the disagreement between the ברייתות in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the two ברייתות disagree about הואיל ואישתני אישתני, making it a dispute between תנאים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Proposed yes: the ברייתא allowing יבום rejects the principle, and the ברייתא forbidding יבום accepts it.
steps.raayaObject: The proposal that הואיל ואישתני אישתני is itself a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two ברייתות on a טומטום's widow (יבום allowed vs. only חליצה), read on the assumption that both follow רבי עקיבא

steps.title: Both sides agree on the principle; the split is רבי אליעזר versus רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the ברייתות argue about הואיל ואישתני אישתני. Everyone accepts it. The ברייתא allowing יבום follows רבי אליעזר, and the one forbidding יבום follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds that once something has changed, it may have changed in other ways too. This ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, and that ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'No' to its own suggestion from the last step. It offers a different reason why the two ברייתות give different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות worry that the טומטום may also be a סריס חמה. They differ only about what follows if he is one. רבי אליעזר allows יבום with a סריס חמה's wife, so the first ברייתא allows יבום. רבי עקיבא does not, so the second ברייתא allows only חליצה. This drops the earlier assumption (step 17) that both ברייתות follow רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
We say / we apply (the principle)
This one... and that one... (assigning each source to a different authority)
The תנא who holds that the wife of a סריס חמה can have יבום

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the principle הואיל ואישתני אישתני is being rejected. Here everyone accepts it. The argument has simply moved to a different question: the law of a סריס חמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps הואיל ואישתני אישתני as a principle everyone shares. It moves the disagreement to the known dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: No; everyone agrees that we say
phrases.notes: Rejects the suggestion from step 18

phrases.english: since he has changed, he has changed (in other ways too)
phrases.notes: So both ברייתות worry he may be a סריס חמה

phrases.english: this one is Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that allows יבום

phrases.english: and that one is Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that allows only חליצה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 18's claim that the תנאים argue about הואיל ואישתני אישתני, and reassigns the two ברייתות to different תנאים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתות argue about הואיל ואישתני אישתני. It also drops the assumption that both follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The different rulings can be explained by the known dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא about a סריס חמה. There is no need to invent a new dispute about the principle.

steps.title: Which תנא holds like רבי עקיבא here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the ברייתא that follows רבי עקיבא, saying the widow of a טומטום does חליצה but not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who holds according to רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who could be the author of the ברייתא that follows רבי עקיבא. This question sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That ברייתא requires חליצה, so it treats the טומטום as only possibly a סריס חמה. If he were surely one, רבי עקיבא would say there is no חליצה either. So the גמרא needs a תנא who follows רבי עקיבא and also sees a טומטום as only a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Which תנא (authored this teaching)?
According to the view of...

phrases.english: And who is the tanna who holds according to Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: Who requires חליצה but not יבום for a טומטום's widow

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 19 by asking who exactly authored the ברייתא that follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא follows רבי עקיבא on סריס חמה and also treats a טומטום as only a doubtful סריס חמה, so that his widow needs חליצה but not יבום.

steps.title: It cannot be רבי יהודה, who treats such a person as a definite סריס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי יהודה and rejects him. In a משנה he rules that a טומטום who was opened and found male does not do חליצה, because he counts as a סריס. That would mean no חליצה at all, which does not fit the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is רבי יהודה, he treats this person as a definite סריס! As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, a טומטום who was torn open and found to be male does not do חליצה, because he is like a סריס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible author, רבי יהודה. It quickly rules him out by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, even a טומטום found to be male counts as a definite סריס. Under רבי עקיבא, a definite סריס חמה's widow needs neither יבום nor חליצה. But our ברייתא does require חליצה, so its author cannot be רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a proposal that will be rejected)
A definite סריס, not just a doubtful one
He treats him as / considers him
As we learned in a משנה
Was torn open (the skin covering the organs was opened)

steps.confusionAlert: Calling him a definite סריס makes the ruling more lenient, not stricter. A definite סריס חמה under רבי עקיבא means no חליצה at all. Our ברייתא requires חליצה, so it must see the case as only a doubt.

phrases.english: If you say it is Rabbi Yehuda —
phrases.notes: The first suggestion for the author

phrases.english: but he considers him a definite eunuch!
phrases.notes: So there would be no חליצה at all

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna, Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: משנה in יבמות

phrases.english: A tumtum who was torn open and found to be male —
phrases.notes: His covering was opened and male organs were found

phrases.english: he may not perform ḥalitza,
phrases.notes: Like a definite סריס חמה, who has no חליצה

phrases.english: because he is like a eunuch!
phrases.notes: This proves רבי יהודה treats him as a definite סריס

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָא וַדַּאי סָרִיס מְשַׁוֵּי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 20's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out רבי יהודה as the author of the ברייתא that follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה treats a טומטום as a definite סריס. Under רבי עקיבא that means no חליצה, which contradicts the ברייתא requiring חליצה.

steps.title: The author is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who treats it as a doubt
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He says a טומטום does not do חליצה because perhaps he will be opened and found to be a סריס חמה. To him it is only a possibility, so the widow needs חליצה out of doubt, but not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says, a טומטום does not do חליצה, because perhaps he will be torn open and found to be a סריס חמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the author is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. It proves this from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is שֶׁמָּא, 'perhaps.' For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, a טומטום is only possibly a סריס חמה. Because of that doubt, following רבי עקיבא, his widow needs חליצה just in case, and יבום is not allowed. This fits the ברייתא exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings the correct answer)
As it is taught in a ברייתא
Perhaps, it might be (shows a doubt, not a certainty)
A man born unable to have children (a natural סריס)
רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה; a תנא

steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות accept הואיל ואישתני אישתני. The one allowing יבום follows רבי אליעזר. The one allowing only חליצה follows רבי עקיבא, as taught by רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He treats a טומטום as only possibly a סריס חמה, so his widow needs חליצה because of the doubt, but may not do יבום.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole סוגיא turns on the difference between 'definitely a סריס' (רבי יהודה) and 'maybe a סריס' (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה). The ruling of חליצה without יבום only makes sense when the case is a doubt.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: The correct author

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
phrases.notes: Proof from a ברייתא

phrases.english: A tumtum does not perform ḥalitza,
phrases.notes: For his brother's widow, since his חליצה might not count

phrases.english: since perhaps he will be torn open and found to be a congenital eunuch.
phrases.notes: 'Perhaps' means only a doubt, which fits a ruling of חליצה without יבום

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out רבי יהודה in step 21, gives the correct author and proves it from a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא following רבי עקיבא is by רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He treats a טומטום as only possibly a סריס חמה, which explains why his widow needs חליצה but not יבום.

steps.title: Why mention only the סריס חמה worry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's reason. Why worry only that the טומטום will be a סריס חמה? Is every טומטום who is opened found to be male? He could be female too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that every טומטום who is opened up is found to be male, and none is ever found to be female?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's reason from the previous step. He mentioned only one worry, and the גמרא asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said a טומטום does not do חליצה because he might turn out to be a סריס חמה. That worry only makes sense if the טומטום is male. But a טומטום could just as easily be opened and found to be female, and a female obviously cannot do חליצה. So why does his reason skip the more basic doubt?

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a rhetorical challenge word)
who is torn / opened (the טומטום's covering skin is cut open)
is found
female

phrases.english: Is that to say that every one who is torn open
phrases.notes: Refers to a טומטום whose covering skin is opened.

phrases.english: is found to be male, and is not found to be female?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical. Obviously some are found to be female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 22 for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's reason: 'perhaps he will be found to be a סריס חמה.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason assumes the טומטום is male. It ignores the more obvious doubt that he may be female.

steps.title: The word 'perhaps' includes two doubts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's 'perhaps' covers more than one doubt. Perhaps the טומטום will be found to be female. And even if male, perhaps he will be a סריס חמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said 'perhaps,' meaning: perhaps he will be opened and found to be female. Or, even if he is male, perhaps he will be found to be a סריס חמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. It explains that his word 'perhaps' was meant to cover both doubts, not only the סריס חמה one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer reads the reason as a chain of doubts. First doubt: maybe female, so no חליצה. Second doubt: even if male, maybe a סריס חמה, so still no חליצה. He mentioned the second doubt explicitly to show that even finding him male does not solve the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: He said 'perhaps,' meaning the word includes several possibilities
he will be torn open
or alternatively / or else
a person born unable to have children (a natural eunuch), who does not do יבום or חליצה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה ignored the possibility of female. His 'perhaps' already includes it. The סריס חמה worry is an extra layer that applies even if he turns out male.

phrases.english: He said 'perhaps' (covering several doubts):
perhaps he will be opened and found to be female.
Or alternatively, even if he is male,
perhaps he will be found to be a natural eunuch.
phrases.notes: This was the part of his statement quoted earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording: 'perhaps' covers more than one doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה worried only about a סריס חמה, so he must assume every טומטום is male.
steps.terutzMaskana: He worries about both doubts: maybe female, and even if male, maybe a סריס חמה.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two views?
steps.stepSummary: Both רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה say a טומטום does not do חליצה. The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between them, and רבא begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them? רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. Then it introduces רבא, whose answer comes on the next amud. This is a setup line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים reach the same result: a טומטום does not do חליצה. But their reasons are different. רבי יהודה treats him as a definite סריס, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה works from doubts. The גמרא wants to know in what case the different reasons give a different ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?
רבא, an אמורא who will give the answer

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: Between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line. רבא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's reason is clear, the גמרא compares it with רבי יהודה's view from step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case in which רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה would rule differently, since both say a טומטום does not do חליצה.
